question: The 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) added three new words to the Preamble i.e. socialist, secular and _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**integrity**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976)** added three new words to the Preamble i.e. **socialist, secular and** **integrity**.
 
• This amendment aimed to emphasize the commitment of the Indian state to uphold the values of socialism, secularism, and integrity in the functioning of the government.
 
• The Preamble reflects the ideals and aspirations that the Constitution of India seeks to achieve.
 
• The addition of these words was meant to **highlight the importance of maintaining unity and integrity in the nation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and came into effect on** 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The **Constitution of India** is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is one of the most comprehensive amendments and is sometimes referred to as a "**mini-Constitution**" due to its wide-ranging impact.
